# Crew API: responses (Public endpoints)

Part of the [Crew API reference](README.md).

## POST /v1/responses

Run a turn.

| About | This endpoint |
|---|---|
| Status | Available now: owner only |
| Tier | Public |
| Stability | preview |
| Callers the API defines | The owner, with the owner's own sign-in. An app, with a credential that holds the scope `responses:write`. |

Not served yet:

- Request body fields: `background`, `input[].content[].type=input_file`, `input[].content[].type=input_image`, `input[].type=function_call_output`, `input[].type=mcp_approval_response`, `reasoning.summary`, `text.format.type=json_schema`, `tool_choice=none`, `tools`.
- Request headers: `Idempotency-Key`.
- Response headers: `X-Crew-Quota-Limit`, `X-Crew-Quota-Remaining`, `X-Crew-Quota-Reset`.

stream=true returns text/event-stream; background=true returns queued at once. Delegated credential: model must be the template id of the app's capability bundle, \<client_id>/\<bundle.agent.id>, or a Bot the grant allows, and conversation must be one opened under this grant. Spends credits against the grant quota; a retry with the same Idempotency-Key is not charged again. Phase 1 accepts text only; `input_image`, `input_file`, `text.format: json_schema` and `reasoning.summary` are phase 2 and open per agent as capabilities reports; when the agent does not support one, 422 capability_unavailable. When json_schema validation fails the whole turn is failed with error.code structured_output_invalid. In the preview, a turn that fair admission refuses answers 200 with status failed and the capacity message. Proposed amendments, 2026-11-26, waiting for a maintainer's sign-off: (1) A turn that continues a conversation is given the conversation's earlier turns as context ahead of its input: the turns that completed and are stored, with their texts as stored (redacted), and without the `instructions` of an earlier turn. A turn that failed, was cancelled, was cut short or was not stored is not given. (2) The earlier turns and the new input together must fit one prompt, 100 KiB (UTF-8), the limit one request's input already has; past it the turn is 413 payload_too_large and the conversation cannot be continued. (3) The stored response of a turn that ran in a conversation is kept as long as that conversation is: 30 days after the conversation's latest turn ended, not 30 days after the turn itself. So a conversation in use keeps every turn it gives. What it gives a later turn is bounded by the 100 KiB of (2). What it keeps is not: each stored turn stays within the limits a stored response already has (1 MiB of request, 1 MiB of reply), and a turn that did not complete is stored with the conversation although it is not given. (4) `previous_response_id` continues the conversation that response ran in, at its end; it does not branch from that response. A response stored before conversations were served ran in none, and naming it is 400 invalid_request. (5) The turns of one conversation may name different models; each turn's `model` is judged on its own. (6) In a conversation, a request whose input texts and ignored field names together are larger than 1 MiB is 413 payload_too_large and is not run: it could not be stored, so no later turn could be given it. A request that large which names no conversation is run as before and starts none: its Response carries no `conversation`.

## GET /v1/responses/{response_id}

Read a turn; can resume its stream.

| About | This endpoint |
|---|---|
| Status | Available now: owner only |
| Tier | Public |
| Stability | preview |
| Callers the API defines | The owner, with the owner's own sign-in. An app, with a credential that holds the scope `conversations:read` or `responses:write`. |

Not served yet:

- Response headers: `X-Crew-Quota-Limit`, `X-Crew-Quota-Remaining`, `X-Crew-Quota-Reset`.

Holding either conversations:read or responses:write is enough; with only responses:write, only responses this grant created can be read. Stream events are stored with the response, so the stream can be resumed. Retention: stored responses (with the stream events used to resume), the event index, resolved approvals and uploaded files are all kept 30 days by default; the owner can set `crew_api.retention_days` in the crew settings to 1 to 365 days. Deleting a conversation deletes its responses and events. After the retention period this returns 404 not_found. Proposed amendments, 2026-11-25, waiting for a maintainer's sign-off: (1) The events themselves are not stored. For a turn that was answered as a stream, the text of each of its deltas is stored and the same events are made from it again when the stream is read. A turn that was answered as JSON has no stream to store; its stream is built from the stored Response. (2) A turn that is still running reads in_progress with no output, and with stream=true its two opening events are sent and the stream closes: the rest of a running stream cannot be followed yet. (3) The `crew_api.retention_days` setting is not built yet: a response is kept 30 days. (4) A query value the parameters do not allow is 400 invalid_request. (5) A turn whose reply text is larger than 1 MiB (UTF-8), or whose input texts and ignored field names together, as sent, are larger than 1 MiB, is answered as ever and is not stored: reading it returns 404 not_found. The limits are the same for a turn answered as JSON and one answered as a stream. Proposed amendment, 2026-11-26, waiting for a maintainer's sign-off: (6) A turn that ran in a conversation is kept as long as that conversation, 30 days after the conversation's latest turn ended, and reads 404 not_found once the conversation's retention is over; its input items follow the same rule.

Path parameters:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `response_id` | string | yes | resp_ id |

Query parameters:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `stream` | boolean | no | true resumes the stream as SSE. |
| `starting_after` | integer | no | Resume after the Nth stream event (sequence_number). |
